facts.text: Founded by German immigrant Martin Loy around 1795, Loysburg grew around his farm, flour mill, and general store.
The town briefly became Pattonville in 1844 when James Patton bought key properties, but locals restored the original name in 1864.
Loysburg sits at the southern end of Morrisons Cove, where the terrain shifts from valleys to the Nittany Anticlinorium’s northeast‑southwest trending anticline.
Yellow Creek, draining 69.2 square miles, flows through Loysburg and sustains a steady 46.8 cfs base flow before joining the Susquehanna Basin.
The historic Loysburg Mill, rebuilt in 1836‑37, operated until 1950, serving as a local landmark for over a century.
The community lies along Pennsylvania Route 36, a historic corridor that follows the Loysburg Gap through Tussey Mountain.
